hits.title: HappyRobot raises $150M for enterprise AI agents
hits.snippet: HappyRobot, a Madrid and New York startup building autonomous AI agents for enterprise operations, has raised 150 million dollars in a Series C round that values the company at 1.2 billion dollars. The financing, announced on 4 August, was led by Prysm Capital and Eurazeo and pushes the firm’s total raised to roughly 200 million dollars. The round lands squarely in the year’s dominant investment theme, agentic software that does work rather than merely drafting it. HappyRobot’s agents place phone calls, schedule appointments, handle data entry and coordinate logistics across voice, email and back-office systems, and the company counts DHL and Uber among its customers. ## Logistics as the proving ground Freight and delivery give agentic AI an unusually concrete test. A logistics desk fields a constant stream of check calls, appointment changes and status requests, the repetitive voice and email work that HappyRobot’s agents are built to absorb. Clearing that queue frees human dispatchers for the exceptions, and it produces the kind of measurable time savings that make a purchase order easy to sign.
